title: Exposure for Games with AI Use
author: Tall_Illustrator5116
selftext:
One thing I didn't really consider when incorporating AI into my games is the effect it will have on exposure. It will of course have an impact on sales and the perception of the game to some people but it will also most certainly effect the amount of exposure you can get organically.

My games which are I would say are a lot better than like 50% of the stuff posted on gametrailers and indie games hub (subjective of course but from a graphical stand point this is true) will not get posted on these channels. It seems a lot of the bigger channels and organisations are quite anti ai, probably in both their personnel and the fear of backlash from anti-ai people and I think this also extends to streamers and youtubers. These fucktard channels like ign, best indie games and indie games hub will never publish your content if you have any mention of ai, so it's definitely something to consider.

Admittedly it's not going make or break your game as you can still get some exposure organically or if you pay for ads but the organic exposure will be more limited than if you didn't have ai. I don't believe some of the stupid numbers people put out about how much it will effect the sales of your game but for sure it will have an effect and I do think it is heavily influenced by genre; pixel art games or stuff like incrementals will have a much greater impact on sales if you use ai. It's clear however the mass market doesn't care too much with games like the finals but as most of us are indie devs it will have a greater effect. Anyway something to consider if your trying to make a commercial game.

comments.author: Crushcha
comments.body: So what's the takeaway? Use AI sparingly or don't mention it at all?

replies.author: Tall_Illustrator5116
replies.body:
I would say if your trying to make a commercial product and want it to be as successful as possible either don't use ai or make it so the ai use is undetectable; no ai music, no ai art and don't disclose the undetectable ai.

If the financials are not your top priority then I don't think it matters either way.

replies.author: Crushcha
replies.body: I think the sad thing is some ppl use it in small ways to speed up their workflow, and then get discredited despite putting years of work

replies.author: Tall_Illustrator5116
replies.body: Ye if that's the case you just should not mention it, there's no benefit there.

comments.body: don't recommend saying it. just release the game and get plrs

replies.author: OriginlessGamer
replies.body: When I uploaded mine, it was just a voluntary disclosure, unless you have clear AI visuals like I do, there's no way to tell, the code can be fully AI written

replies.author: Crushcha
replies.body: Its just I've heard things about how games can be taken down if it turns out you didn't disclose it and found out....but really curious if that has actually happened before or not

replies.author: Tall_Illustrator5116
replies.body: It doesn't it's a good faith disclosure, most companies are using AI to code nowadays and they don't disclose

comments.author: OriginlessGamer
comments.body:
I definitely got some backslash in terms of AI in my game, my demo on itch ( [https://originlessgamer.itch.io/slots-and-shots](https://originlessgamer.itch.io/slots-and-shots) ) is currently at 146 views and 16 plays and also 16 wishlists on Steam in \~7 days.

In my case, I don't think the issue is the AI, I think it's the game niche (casino sim), that's why any algorithm is absolutely refusing to give it any organic traffic 😄 

Back to the AI topic, I think opinions are divided, on the one hand there's Anti-AI crowd and the witch hunt is strong, on the other hand, I had "familiy and friends" and also strangers say that the graphics are alright. 

I actually made a video about it [https://youtu.be/Umq8KiSNmu4](https://youtu.be/Umq8KiSNmu4)

What's your game by the way, can you share a link?

replies.author: Tall_Illustrator5116
replies.body:
Sorry its an alt account, don't want it to link to my games due to what I've said. 

No offence but this is not really the type of game I'm talking about, it's more where it's a serious commercial product with 1000s of hours of development and it's using AI for small areas. The product you've developed looks more or less completely built with AI and realistically will not sell well. Not there's anything wrong with that but it's a different product.

replies.author: OriginlessGamer
replies.body: got it, no worries. Here's another guy talking about AI in professional game dev (not the kind of shit I made), I think this can be more relevant: [https://youtu.be/e4YvWGiB0UQ](https://youtu.be/e4YvWGiB0UQ)

replies.author: rnostvac
replies.body:
Yes the art, color scheme and interface elements all look nice. Haven't tried it yet but looks like a fun little game.

Not sure what the haters expect from a solo developer or even a small indie team but obviously not everyone can afford to hire an artist nor have the time to become one, but of course Antis don't care for logic or reason only to can rage.

comments.author: LeafyWolf
comments.body:
Skate to where the puck will be.  Anti-AI sentiment in the gamer community is such a footgun.  The same people who are complaining about release dates being decades are complaining about AI use.  

Eventually, AI won't be the de jour thing to hate, and AI gaming will be ubiquitous.  The successful AI games being developed now will be released next year.

replies.author: Tall_Illustrator5116
replies.body: Very true, at this point it will lessen sales a bit but not hugely and that will continue to lessen as time goes on but I do think it will have an impact for years to come and again I do think it is genre dependent, I don't think for AAA games it will have much of an impact but for sure it will be greater for indie games.

comments.author: bingewavecinema
comments.body:
So marketing, whether your game is AI or not, it the biggest and hardest par tto game development.

Most games don't have a strategy beyond posting in subbreddits when they need to understand influencers, socials, ads and reddit.

I've promoted quite a bit of games; MOST people don't care if its AI or not, just the load obnxous people who are moslty on Reddit.

replies.author: Tall_Illustrator5116
replies.body:
I would agree to an extent, the game will always be the main factor to whether a game is successful, if the game is amazing or original it will almost always do well regardless of the marketing.

What I'm talking about is games releasing with serious commercial aspirations (not AAA); 10,000 plus sales with marketing budgets behind them i.e professional game devs. These games will certainly have a marketing strategy. 

As per my post the exposure your game gets will definitely be effected by AI use and in turn that will also have an effect on sales although to what extent is very variable depending on genre and other factors.
